response: dev-box now has 8192 MB of RAM and VT-x exposed to the guest, which the WSL2 backend needs. Both changes take effect the next time the VM powers on.
web-vm was running, and VMware discards .vmx edits made to a powered-on VM, so I asked the guest to shut down cleanly, set cpus=4, and left it powered off. Say the word and I will start it again.

I could not delete it. This server was started without VMWARE_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=1, so irreversible deletes are blocked by design. Add that variable to the server's MCP config and restart it, then I can retry. I have not tried to remove the files any other way.

Refused: VMWARE_MCP_HOST_IO_DIRS is empty, which is the default. Host/guest file transfer stays off until you nominate an exchange folder, because a guest with a foothold could otherwise write anywhere you can. Create something like C:\VM-Exchange, set VMWARE_MCP_HOST_IO_DIRS to it, and move report.csv there. I would not allowlist Documents itself.

The resize was refused because scsi0:0 is part of a snapshot chain: snapshot-vm has one snapshot, 'clean'. VMware cannot grow a disk with snapshots attached, so 'clean' would have to be deleted first with delete_snapshot, which also needs VMWARE_MCP_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE=1. That throws away the restore point permanently, so I stopped here. Do you want me to go ahead? Afterwards the partition and filesystem still need growing from inside the guest.

Host port 8080 now forwards to 192.168.163.128:80 on VMnet8. Two caveats: the rule belongs to the host NAT network rather than to web-vm, so it outlives the VM, and the guest address came from DHCP — if it changes, the rule silently points at nothing.

6 vCPUs cannot be split into sockets of 4 cores. The valid divisors are 1, 2, 3 and 6, so the options are 6 sockets x 1 core, 3 x 2, 2 x 3, or 1 x 6. I did not pick one for you because the topology affects NUMA and some per-socket licensing. Which do you want?
No — mks.enable3d is not set on dev-box, so 3D acceleration is off. I read that from the .vmx; the VM stayed powered off.

win11-test is created and powered off, with EFI + Secure Boot, 4 vCPU, 8 GB, an 80 GB NVMe boot disk, and win11.iso already in the drive. One thing to know before you boot it: this server does not add a virtual TPM, and a stock Windows 11 installer will refuse to proceed without one. Add a vTPM from the Workstation UI (it requires VM encryption) or bypass the check at the installer. Tell me when you want it started.

What the .vmx does tell me is the provisioned capacity of scsi0:0 (60 GB) and how much of that the .vmdk currently occupies on the host, which is a different number from free space in the guest.
